issues.legal_issue: An owner may take possession of premises after the tenant vacates them without first obtaining permission from the rent-control authority.
material_facts: The tenant vacated the premises and surrendered possession to the owner.
The owner took possession and moved into the premises.
The owner informed the authorities that the premises had been vacated and that he was occupying them.
issues.conclusion: The owner’s occupation was not unlawful; the rent-control provision did not prevent a landlord from taking possession after a tenant vacated.
issues.legal_principle: Section 7 of the U.P. (Temporary) Control of Rent and Eviction Act, 1947 provides for notification of a vacancy and permits the District Magistrate to regulate a landlord’s letting of vacant premises, but it does not bar the landlord from taking possession after the tenant has vacated.

predicates.tenant_vacated: The tenant ceased occupying the premises and vacated them.
predicates.owner_took_possession: The owner accepted possession of the premises after the tenant vacated.
predicates.owner_occupied_premises: The owner moved into and actually occupied the premises.

issues.definition: When the tenant vacates, the owner takes possession, and the owner occupies the premises, the owner’s occupation is lawful.

issues.legal_issue: A public authority cannot requisition premises in actual occupation without inquiring into whether suitable alternative accommodation exists for the occupant and giving the occupant an opportunity to address that question.
material_facts: The owner had moved into and was actually occupying the premises when they were requisitioned.
The owner had told the authorities that his other residence was inadequate and insanitary.

The requisition order treated the owner’s other residence as sufficient reason not to provide alternative accommodation, without an inquiry into whether suitable alternative accommodation existed or an opportunity for the owner to address the issue.
issues.conclusion: The requisition order was illegal and was quashed because the authority failed to ascertain through an inquiry, with an opportunity for the occupant to be heard, whether suitable alternative accommodation existed for the occupant’s needs.
issues.legal_principle: The second proviso to section 3 of the U.P. (Temporary) Accommodation Requisition Act, 1947 bars requisition of premises in actual occupation unless the District Magistrate forms an opinion that suitable alternative accommodation exists for the occupant’s needs or has been provided. Because that opinion concerns a fact requiring ascertainment, natural justice, including the audi alteram partem principle, requires an inquiry and an opportunity for the occupant to be heard. The Court applied A. K. Kraipak v. Union of India, [1970] 1 S.C.R. 457, on the application of natural justice to administrative decision-making.

rule.if: requisition_proceeding and premises_actually_occupied and alternative_accommodation_condition_applies and (no_fact_finding_inquiry or no_occupant_opportunity)

predicates.requisition_proceeding: A public authority is deciding whether to requisition premises.
predicates.premises_actually_occupied: A person is actually occupying the premises when the authority considers requisitioning them.
predicates.alternative_accommodation_condition_appl: The authority must determine whether suitable alternative accommodation exists or has been provided for the occupant’s needs before requisitioning the occupied premises.
predicates.no_fact_finding_inquiry: The authority does not investigate the facts needed to determine whether suitable alternative accommodation exists or has been provided.
predicates.no_occupant_opportunity: The authority does not give the occupant an opportunity to address whether suitable alternative accommodation exists or has been provided.

issues.definition: When an authority considers requisitioning premises in actual occupation and must determine whether suitable alternative accommodation exists or has been provided, failure to investigate that fact or hear the occupant makes the requisition order invalid.
